# Reproducibility of R code {#sec-reproducibility}

All analytical steps and standalone output scripts in this repository are written in R, and this documentation book is rendered with Quarto following FAIR data and research software practices [@Wilkinson_2016; @Barker_2022].

The block below reports the active R and Quarto versions used to render this book:

```{r}
library(quarto)
R.version
quarto_version()
```

## Installing development packages from GitHub

In addition to CRAN packages (`dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `stringr`, `foreach`, `foreign`, `ggplot2`, `cowplot`, `DT`, `sf`, `terra`, `fasterize`, `units`, `here`, `XML`), this workflow depends on two R packages installed directly from GitHub:

- `Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/ecoSynthesis` [@ecoSynthesis_pkg] — cross-referencing classes, agreement, entropy, plotting, and synthesis functions;
- `Global-Ecosystems-Atlas/geco` — standard Global Ecosystems Atlas pixel values and colour tables for IUCN GET functional groups.

```{r}
#| eval: false
pak::pak("Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/ecoSynthesis")
pak::pak("Global-Ecosystems-Atlas/geco")
```

## FAIR software assessment

This repository tracks progress against the ARDC FAIR Software Checklist v0.2 via automated checks in `.fair/fair_check.R` and `.fair/fair-checklist.yml`, with the latest score summary and gap breakdown published in the repository `README.md` (`fair/fair-score.json` and `fair/fair-scores.png`).
